speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the reply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think there was a recent report which 	showed that Singaporeans, in general, spend about 3.4 years of trying to conceive before finally getting help when they cannot.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And we know as well that the trend is that Singaporeans are getting married later in life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask: one, whether MOH is looking into how to create more awareness about the importance and the need for fertility testing at a younger age; and two, I really think that price might be a factor and so I am hoping that subsidies can be extended to all, rather than a selective few?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will answer his second question first in respect of the funds and subsidies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I have mentioned, these tests are medically indicated.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It means that, if the patient or the couple goes to the doctor, they will then recommend the specific test that the patient requires, based on their conditions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, in that sense, there are already sufficient subsidies that ensure that if they need the support, they need the help, they will get the subsidies needed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The issue is they are not going to get the help needed and I think that is an important point you raised.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is something that we need to continue looking at.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I believe that with various efforts by different partners who are also supporting this message, hopefully, there will be greater awareness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think there are a few things that we can perhaps leverage on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have organisations, like "I Love Children", which also encourages checking for fertility treatments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And as we are also rolling out our Marriage and Parenthood packages, these also opportunities for us to encourage couples to take note of these things.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am also thinking that with Healthier SG, especially if it continues to be rolled out to the younger groups, you have opportunity for more individualised healthcare plan.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Through these channels, we hope to see better awareness and people are more encouraged to then check on their fertility status.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is back to the subsidies again because I do think it is important.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I just ask whether MOH has done a cost benefit analysis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know I am always asking Government to spend more, but perhaps, if we spend more in getting people to do their fertility screening at a younger age, we might then spend less in providing subsidies for IVF treatment, which is even more expensive and which costs the Government quite a fair bit currently.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am glad the Member asked that question.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, in that sense, there is no cost-effectiveness to roll it out at that level.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think it is something we will continue to monitor and when the evidence changes or if there is some data to the contrary, these are the things that we can look at.
